texts: bad: two things go wrong - "shield a cove from north winds" is read as the winds being where the shielding came from rather than what it wards off, and the burning is keyed to the lantern instead of to each shielding, so repeated shieldings of one cove collapse into a single burning. Rewrite as: "Whenever cliff-spires shield a cove against north winds, every lantern in that cove burns stably through winter while that shielding lasts." - "against" kills the origin reading, "every lantern" reaches each lantern individually, and "while that shielding lasts" ties one burning to each shielding. ("Through winter" is recorded only as a time, not as lasting the whole season; that is a known limitation no rewrite fixes.)

bad: this rule can never fire - the passive condition ("a cove is blocked ... by cliff-spires") became a trigger built out of an invented blocking term that no fact can ever match, so nothing will ever set it off; on top of that "blocked from the north wind" reads as a spatial origin, and "the lanterns in that cove" never reaches the individual lanterns. Rewrite as: "Whenever cliff-spires shield a cove against the north wind, every lantern in that cove stays lit through winter." - an active condition clause with an explicit subject gives the trigger something real to match, "against" removes the origin reading, and "every lantern" hands the staying-lit to each lantern.
good. the name, the cove kind, the "shielded" property and containment in Aelmere are all recorded, with nothing invented.

bad: "in cold winds" is filed as the *place* the going-out happens - a wind treated as a location - rather than as the circumstance under which it never happens. Rewrite as: "Northcove lanterns never go out when cold winds blow." - a finite "when" clause puts the circumstance where a reasoner can match it against an actual wind.
